### 4. workspace-fork-apply-security-hardening

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Three distinct gaps, all confirmed live in the current tree. (1) `DirectoryCopyExclusions` (`src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationBundleTools.cs:25-35`) only excludes build/VCS noise directories (`.git`, `.vs`, `bin`, `obj`, ...) — `CopyDirectory` (`ValidationBundleTools.cs:303-322`) copies every FILE unconditionally via `Directory.EnumerateFiles` + `File.Copy`, so `.env`, `appsettings.*.json`, `*.pubxml`, `secrets.json` etc. land verbatim inside `<workspace>/.roslynmcp/forks/<ts>-<slug>/`, a server-writable directory outside source control review. (2) `retention="keep"` (`ValidationBundleTools.cs:111`) has no expiry path — `ShouldRetainFork` (`:251-258`) returns `true` unconditionally for `keep` and nothing ever revisits `.roslynmcp/forks/` afterward, so kept forks (each a full workspace copy, potentially containing the leaked secrets from gap 1) accumulate indefinitely. `RestoreForkAsync` (`:324-369`) additionally hardcodes `FileName = "dotnet"` and a fixed 2-minute restore timeout with no override. (3) `test_coverage` (`TestCoverageTools.cs:60`) allocates `coverageDir = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "roslyn-mcp-coverage", Guid.NewGuid())` and never deletes it after `ParseAndAggregateCoberturaXml` (`:82`) runs — every invocation leaks a temp directory containing `coverage.cobertura.xml` files. Not bundled with peer `workspace-fork-apply-robustness-cancellation`: verified against Rule 1's four conditions — that peer's fixes (CancellationToken plumbing through `CopyDirectory`/`DeleteDirectoryIfExists`, OCE-vs-timeout misclassification in `TestCoverageTools.cs:86-94`, concurrent-fork race) are a distinct root cause (cooperative cancellation) from this initiative's root cause (secret exposure + unbounded retention + temp leak). Both touch `CopyDirectory` and `TestCoverageTools.cs` but at non-overlapping code sites, a single fix does not resolve both symptom sets, and the regression test for one (cancellation mid-copy) does not exercise the other (secret-pattern exclusion) — condition 1 (same code path) is arguably shared at the file level but conditions 2 and 3 fail outright, so `ruleOneBundleResolved: split` per Rule 1's "when any condition is uncertain, keep rows separate." |
| Approach | (1) In `ValidationBundleTools.cs`, extend the exclusion mechanism from a flat directory-name `HashSet` to also filter FILES by a glob/suffix pattern list (add a `SecretFilePatterns` array — `.env`, `.env.*`, `appsettings.*.json` minus `appsettings.json`/`appsettings.Development.json` base template caveat — actually exclude any `appsettings.*.json` except keep a documented allowlist, `*.pubxml`, `*.pubxml.user`, `secrets.json`, `*.pfx`, `*.key`) and apply it inside `CopyDirectory`'s file-copy loop (`:307-311`) via a small `IsSecretBearingFile(string fileName)` helper, mirroring the existing `DirectoryCopyExclusions.Contains` check used for directories at `:315`. (2) Add an expiry/cleanup path for `retention="keep"` forks: on `CreateForkDirectory` (`:272-282`), before creating the new fork, sweep `.roslynmcp/forks/` for existing entries older than a configurable TTL (env var `ROSLYNMCP_FORK_TTL_HOURS`, default 24h, parsed from the fork directory's `yyyyMMddTHHmmssfffZ` timestamp prefix already embedded in the slug) and delete them via the existing `CleanupFork`/`DeleteDirectoryIfExists`-style logic — this is a lazy sweep-on-create, not a background timer, keeping the change edit-only and dependency-free. Make `RestoreForkAsync`'s dotnet path and timeout configurable via optional parameters sourced from env vars (`ROSLYNMCP_FORK_DOTNET_PATH` default `"dotnet"`, `ROSLYNMCP_FORK_RESTORE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` default `2`), read once at the top of `RestoreForkAsync` (`:324-329`) rather than introducing a new IOptions binding (no existing options-binding infra in this codebase for tool-level config — smallest complete fix per directive #6). (3) In `TestCoverageTools.cs`, wrap the coverage-dir lifecycle in a `try/finally` around `RunCoveragePassAsync`+aggregation (`:60-84`) that deletes `coverageDir` (if it exists) after `ParseAndAggregateCoberturaXml` returns, mirroring the swallow-non-actionable pattern already used for the fork-kill `catch` in `ValidationBundleTools.cs:358`. |

Test files (≤2): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ValidationBundleToolsTests.cs` (extend with secret-exclusion + TTL-sweep cases), a new `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestCoverageToolsTests.cs` if one does not already cover `RunTestCoverageCore` (none found by glob — verify at implementation time; add coverage-dir-cleanup assertion). ### 5. workspace-fork-apply-robustness-cancellation

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Two independent robustness gaps confirmed in source. (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationBundleTools.cs:303-322` (`CopyDirectory`) and `:482-500` (`DeleteDirectoryIfExists`) are synchronous, non-cancellable recursive file-tree walks with no `CancellationToken` parameter; `WorkspaceForkApply` (`:103-217`) calls `CopyDirectory(sourceRoot, forkPath)` at `:155` inside a `gate.RunWriteAsync` lambda that DOES receive a token (`c`), but the token is silently dropped at the copy/cleanup boundary — a large solution copy or a large fork cleanup cannot be aborted mid-walk even though the gate believes the call is cancellable. (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/TestCoverageTools.cs:86-94` catches `OperationCanceledException` unconditionally and always returns `BuildTimeoutResult()` — this conflates a genuine caller/session cancellation with `WorkspaceExecutionGate`'s internal `_requestTimeout` deadline (`WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs:70`, armed per-request), so a user-cancelled `test_coverage` call is misreported to the MCP client as "timeout" instead of propagating cancellation. The repo already has the correct pattern for this exact distinction in the same file family: `ValidationBundleTools.cs:353` (`RestoreForkAsync`) uses `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)` to separate the internal 2-minute restore timeout from real cancellation, then rethrows/wraps accordingly — `TestCoverageTools.cs` needs the mirror-image guard. Confirmed via Grep that `CopyDirectory`/`DeleteDirectoryIfExists` are private, single-file, recursively-self-called only (no other call sites) — this is a surgical two-file fix, not a cross-cutting rename. Third acceptance criterion (reject/serialize a second concurrent `workspace_fork_apply` against the same `sourceRoot`) is also confirmed absent: no `SemaphoreSlim`/lock construct exists anywhere in `ValidationBundleTools.cs` today (0 hits), so two concurrent forks of the same source currently race the recursive copy unguarded. |
| Approach | **File 1 — `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationBundleTools.cs`:** (a) add a `CancellationToken ct` parameter to `CopyDirectory` and `DeleteDirectoryIfExists`, threading `c` (the gate-scoped token already available in `WorkspaceForkApply`'s lambda) through both the file-copy loop and the recursive directory descent, calling `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` at the top of each loop iteration (mirrors the existing `ReplayPreviewIntoForkAsync`/`WriteForkFileAsync` token-threading pattern already in this file at `:371-440`). Update the two call sites (`:155`, `:474`) to pass `c`. (b) Add a static `ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim>` keyed by the normalized (case-insensitive, full-path) `sourceRoot`, acquired around the copy+replay+restore section of `WorkspaceForkApply` (`:153-216`) so a second concurrent fork-apply against the same `sourceRoot` waits (serializes) rather than racing the in-flight `CopyDirectory`; release in a `finally`. **File 2 — `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/TestCoverageTools.cs:86-94`:** split the single `catch (OperationCanceledException)` into `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested) { throw; }` (real caller/session cancellation — propagate) followed by the existing unconditional `catch (OperationCanceledException) { ...BuildTimeoutResult... }` (internal gate-timeout path only), exactly mirroring the `when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)` split already proven in `ValidationBundleTools.cs:353-360`. No public signatures change (both edited methods are `private static`/already accept `ct`), so no external caller updates needed. |
| Scope | Production files: 2 — `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ValidationBundleTools.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/TestCoverageTools.cs`. Test files: up to 2 — extend `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ValidationBundleToolsTests.cs` (cancellation aborts `CopyDirectory` mid-walk; concurrent `workspace_fork_apply` against the same `sourceRoot` is rejected/serialized) and add cancellation-vs-timeout coverage in the existing `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/TestCoverageFailureEnvelopeTests.cs` (real `OperationCanceledException` propagates; internal gate timeout still yields the timeout envelope). Within Rule 3 (2 ≤ 4) and Rule 4 (≤2 test files touched, no new files needed) with headroom. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 40000 |
| Risks | (a) Threading `ct` into `CopyDirectory`'s recursive descent must not change existing non-cancelled behavior or copy ordering — verify existing `ValidationBundleToolsTests` fork-apply happy-path assertions still pass unchanged. (b) The new per-`sourceRoot` semaphore must not introduce a deadlock with `gate.RunWriteAsync`'s own per-workspace serialization (`WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs` `RunPerWorkspaceAsync`) — acquire/release must nest correctly and release on all exception paths (including the existing `catch { CleanupFork(...); throw; }` at `:208-215`). (c) Rejected bundle peer `workspace-fork-apply-security-hardening` (DirectoryCopyExclusions secret patterns, fork retention/expiry, coverage-temp-dir cleanup) touches the same file but a disjoint set of functions/symptoms — Rule 1 conditions 1–3 fail (different code paths, no single fix resolves both, tests don't cross-exercise), so it is kept as a separate initiative rather than bundled; both initiatives touching `ValidationBundleTools.cs` should not be scheduled in adjacent parallel-execute waves to avoid a merge conflict on the same file. ### 6. apply-with-verify-cancellation-and-compile-scope

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Two independent bugs in `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs:38-118`, both inside the `gate.RunWriteAsync` closure that runs apply→verify→revert under the linked (caller+timeout) token `c`. **(1) Cancellation swallows the revert.** `preBaseline` (line 47-48), `applyResult` (52), `postCheck` (67-68), and `undoService.RevertAsync` (106) all await on the SAME linked token. If the caller cancels (or the per-request timeout in `WorkspaceExecutionGate` fires) after `applyResult.Success` is true but before `RevertAsync` completes, the awaited call throws `OperationCanceledException` immediately — `RevertAsync` never runs, or runs against a token that is already exhausted/cancelled and aborts mid-revert. The workspace is left mutated with no compensating rollback and no signal to the caller beyond a generic cancellation. This mirrors the class of bug `RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/UndoService.cs` already guards against for its own snapshot capture, but `ApplyWithVerifyTool` has no equivalent guard. **(2) Unscoped compile_check baseline/verify.** Lines 47-48 and 67-68 both call `compileCheckService.CheckAsync(workspaceId, new CompileCheckOptions(), c)` — an empty `CompileCheckOptions()` compiles the FULL solution twice per `apply_with_verify` call, even when the preview touched a single file/project. `RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs:709` (and its sibling at line 745, fed by the `batchProjectFilter` computed at `EditService.cs:138-142`) already establishes the correct pattern: derive the distinct owning-project set of the touched documents, and pass `ProjectFilter` when exactly one project is touched (`null` — i.e. full-solution — when the edit spans more than one project, since a single-project filter would miss cross-project breakage). `ApplyWithVerifyTool` never adopted this scoping when it was extracted as the three-calls-in-one convenience wrapper. |
| Approach | Single file: `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`, method `ApplyWithVerify`. **(A) Project-scoped compile_check:** after `previewStore.PeekWorkspaceId`, call `previewStore.Retrieve(previewToken)` (non-consuming per `IPreviewStore.Retrieve` doc contract) to get `(OriginalSolution, ModifiedSolution)`, compute `ModifiedSolution.GetChanges(OriginalSolution).GetProjectChanges()` and project the distinct project names — mirror `EditService.cs:138-142`'s `ownerProjects`/`batchProjectFilter` pattern exactly (single distinct project → that project name as `ProjectFilter`; 0 or >1 distinct projects → `null`, i.e. unscoped). Pass this filter into BOTH the pre-apply `CompileCheckOptions(ProjectFilter: projectFilter)` (line 47-48) and the post-apply one (line 67-68) so both calls stay consistent. **(B) Cancellation-safe revert:** wrap the region from `applyResult.Success` check through the `RevertAsync` call in a `try { ... } catch (OperationCanceledException) when (applyResult.Success) { ... }` guard (or restructure as apply → try/catch around verify). On catch, do NOT reuse `c` — construct a short-lived, purpose-built `using var revertCts = new CancellationTokenSource(RevertBudget)` (new named constant, e.g. `private static readonly TimeSpan RevertBudget = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);`, sized independently of the caller's original timeout so a slow caller-side cancel doesn't also starve the compensating rollback) and call `await undoService.RevertAsync(workspaceId, revertCts.Token).ConfigureAwait(false)` best-effort (swallow exceptions from the revert attempt itself so the original cancellation still propagates — do not mask a genuine cancel with a revert-path exception). After the best-effort revert, rethrow the original `OperationCanceledException` (via `ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw` or a plain `throw;` inside the catch) so the MCP framework's normal cancellation handling still fires — the fix changes what happens to workspace STATE on cancel, not whether cancellation is honored as an outcome. No behavior change to the non-cancelled apply→verify→revert path (existing rollback-on-new-errors logic at lines 92-118 is untouched). |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ApplyWithVerifyTool.cs`. Test files (1, new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ApplyWithVerifyCancellationAndScopeTests.cs` (no existing dedicated test file for this tool was found — `Grep` across `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests` for `ApplyWithVerify` only hit `Top10V2RegressionTests.cs` and `PreviewTokenStaleAcrossAutoReloadTests.cs`, neither of which owns this tool's behavior). Well within Rule 3 (1 ≤ 4) and Rule 4 (1 ≤ 3); no exemption needed. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 35000 |
| Risks | (1) The revert-budget catch must only fire when `applyResult.Success` is true — a cancellation during the PRE-apply baseline (before `ApplyRefactoringAsync` ran) must propagate as plain cancellation with nothing to revert; verify the guard condition captures this correctly. (2) Swallowing exceptions from the best-effort `RevertAsync` inside the cancellation catch must not also swallow a genuine second-failure signal silently — log it (e.g. via existing `ILogger` if the tool has one, else surface via `AmbientGateMetrics` if that ambient exists in this call path) rather than a bare empty catch, per repo Directive #3 (bad code is never silent — an empty catch here would itself be the anti-pattern this initiative is fixing elsewhere). (3) The `ProjectFilter` derivation via `previewStore.Retrieve` reads `OriginalSolution`/`ModifiedSolution` a second time (the apply path also reads them via `refactoringService.ApplyRefactoringAsync`) — confirm this extra `Retrieve` call is genuinely non-consuming (per `IPreviewStore.Retrieve` XML doc) and does not perturb the token's TTL/version-pinning (`InvalidateOnVersionBump` machinery) before relying on it in production. (4) `EditService.cs`'s existing pattern narrows to `null` (full-solution) when the touched set spans >1 project — same choice made here; confirm this doesn't silently under-scope when a preview's diff spans exactly the project boundary of a partial-class or linked-file split (rare but possible). |
| Validation | New test file exercises: (a) cancellation-after-successful-apply triggers a `RevertAsync` call even when the original `CancellationToken` is already cancelled — assert via a fake `IUndoService`/`IWorkspaceExecutionGate` test double that `RevertAsync` was invoked with a token that is NOT the original cancelled token (i.e. still cancellable/uncancelled at call time); (b) the original `OperationCanceledException` still surfaces to the caller after the revert attempt; (c) `ICompileCheckService.CheckAsync` is invoked (pre- and post-apply) with `ProjectFilter` set to the single project name when the preview's `ModifiedSolution.GetChanges(OriginalSolution)` touches exactly one project, and with `ProjectFilter: null` when it touches zero/multiple; (d) existing happy-path (`status=applied`) and rollback-on-new-errors (`status=rolled_back`) behavior is unchanged — extend/re-verify against `Top10V2RegressionTests.cs` if it already exercises `apply_with_verify`, or add equivalent coverage in the new file.
